previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of atrial fibrillation, diastolic heart failure, severe aortic stenosis, and chronic bronchitis was admitted for worsening shortness of breath and right leg swelling. He was diagnosed with a heart failure exacerbation and cellulitis of the right lower extremity. Treatment included IV furosemide for volume overload, which improved his dyspnea, and vancomycin followed by oral antibiotics for cellulitis. His subtherapeutic digoxin and warfarin levels were corrected, though anticoagulation led to spontaneous hematomas requiring temporary hold of enoxaparin and warfarin. A right shoulder hematoma was identified and managed conservatively with pain control and elevation. Aphthous ulcers were treated with viscous lidocaine. He stabilized, completed a full antibiotic course, and was discharged to extended care with optimized heart failure and anticoagulation management, along with follow-up plans for cardiology and orthopedics.

ACTIVE ISSUES ========= # Dyspnea attributed to diastolic CHF Exacerbation: He has a history of severe aortic stenosis. He appeared to be in volume overload with pulmonary congestion and bilateral leg edema during evaluation prior to admission. Symptoms improved after transfusion 1 unit PRBC with concurrent 40mg IV Lasix in the ED. ___ x3. Was subsequently carefully diuresed. Saturations improved to 95% on RA on the floor, although still symptomatically dyspneic. He was d/c on home oxygen. # Dyspnea, attributed to COPD exacerbation: Dyspnea was felt to be multifactorial. He was noted to have significant wheezing, and was treated with prednisone/azithromycin/duonebs for COPD exacerbation. # RLE Redness: Mildly erythematous compared to left leg but not particularly warm. No pain or evidence of infection. Given lack of fever or leukocytosis, he was not treated with antibiotics. Continued moisturizing with Cetaphil lotion and Sarna along with elevation of legs with ___ stockings. # Anemia: s/p 1 unit PRBC with adequate response. Pt's son reports increasing pallor and dyspnea, which could be consistent with worsening anemia. Given constipation, lack of melena and one guiaiac negative stool, unlikely to be major GI bleed although cannot exclude slow ooze. Hemodynamics stable. Iron panel normal and without labs suggestive of hemolysis. In discussion with PCP, decided NOT to pursue colonoscopy at this time given age and comorbidities. # ___: Creatinine elevated to 1.4 over baseline of 1.0 on admission. Pt with signs of volume overload on CXR and with ___ swelling, so possibly this is related to decreased forward flow. Creatinine improved with diuresis, consistent with cardiorenal syndrome. # AS: Recently seen in cardiology clinic for evaluation for palliative balloon valvuloplasty. This was previously thought to be option but he has a high risk of stroke, and multiple co-morbidities. After family meeting was held, it was decided not to pursue this. Echo obtained showing generally similar findings. # Atrial fibrillation: CHADS2 of 4 (CHF, Age, previous TIA). INR 2.2 on admission. Rate is currently well controlled and unlikely to be contributing to diastolic dysfunction. Continued home warfarin, though stopping it was addressed at the family meeting. However, given his high CHADS score and functional status, continuing it was felt to be important until follow up with Cardiology and further discussion. He was continued on home metoprolol, diltiazem, and digoxin. # CAD: Patient complained of chest pain once several weeks ago, but has not had it since. Unclear if this was exertional pain. Troponins remained flat, and there were no new wall motion abnormalities on echo. He was continued on his home aspirin, metoprolol, and statin. #Goals of care: Multi-disciplinary meeting with palliative care and cardiology and medicine team given natural history of aortic stenosis with his co-morbidities. radiology_notes.text:
RIGHT LOWER EXTREMITY DVT STUDY

INDICATION:  ___ male with right leg swelling and pain.  Evaluate for
evidence of DVT.

COMPARISON:  ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Grayscale, color Doppler, and spectral analysis of the venous
system of the right lower extremity was performed.

FINDINGS:  There is normal compression and augmentation of the common femoral,
proximal superficial femoral, mid superficial femoral, distal superficial
femoral, and popliteal veins in the right lower extremity.  The posterior
tibial and peroneal veins were visualized and demonstrate compression and
wall-to-wall flow.  There is normal phasicity of the common femoral veins
bilaterally.  Soft tissue swelling was noted at the level of the calf.


IMPRESSION:  No evidence of DVT in the right lower extremity.

HISTORY:  Dyspnea on exertion, increased leg swelling.

TECHNIQUE:  Upright AP and lateral views of the chest.

COMPARISON:  ___.

FINDINGS:

Moderate to severe cardiomegaly is unchanged.  The aorta remains tortuous and
diffusely calcified.  Mild to moderate pulmonary edema with perihilar
enlargement and haziness as well as vascular indistinctness is re-
demonstrated, slightly improved compared to the prior study.  There are
persistent small bilateral pleural effusions, larger on the right than the
left, not substantially changed in size.  Bibasilar airspace opacities may
reflect atelectasis, though infection or aspiration cannot be excluded.  There
is no pneumothorax identified.  Extensive degenerative changes of both
shoulders are again demonstrated with high-riding humeral heads.

IMPRESSION:

Mild to moderate congestive heart failure with small bilateral pleural
effusions, slightly improved compared to the prior exam.  Bibasilar airspace
opacities could reflect atelectasis, but infection or aspiration are not
excluded.

REASON FOR EXAMINATION:  Evaluation of the patient with worsening productive
cough and oxygen requirement.

Portable AP radiograph of the chest was reviewed in comparison to examination
___.

There is additional interval progression of moderate interstitial pulmonary
edema associated with bilateral pleural effusions and bibasal consolidations. 
Cardiomediastinal silhouette is unchanged in appearance.  Substantial
degenerative changes of the right shoulder are redemonstrated, better
appreciated on the dedicated view from ___.
